definition: A configuration value set before training begins (such as learning rate or batch size) that is not learned from the data itself.
details: Hyperparameter tuning, via grid search, random search, or Bayesian optimization, is a key part of building effective models.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. Boil it down and it is this: A configuration value set before training begins (such as learning rate or batch size) that is not learned from the data itself. Here is why it matters: Hyperparameter tuning, via grid search, random search, or Bayesian optimization, is a key part of building effective models. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Hyperparameter.
